cards.g: lacking common sense; inconsiderate, out of line
cards.d: 世の中で当たり前とされる考え方やマナーから外れていること。
s: 「お兄ちゃん、こんな時間まで飲み歩くとか非常識じゃない？」
非常識
"Isn't it a bit much, staying out drinking this late?"
夜中の二時に電話をかけてくるなんて、非常識にもほどがある。
非常識
Calling at two in the morning — there's a limit to how inconsiderate you can be.
col: 非常識にもほどがある
cf: Near-synonym; 非常識 is the standard criticism of bad manners or thoughtless behaviour.
cards.note: Usually a judgement of manners, not intelligence: 'out of line' rather than 'irrational'.

cards.d: あれこれと文句や理屈を言うようす。
s: 会議では部下の報告を途中で遮り、「つべこべ言うな、結論から話せ」と威張り散らす。
つべこべ
In meetings he cuts off subordinates' reports halfway and lords it over everyone: "Stop quibbling, give me the conclusion."
つべこべ言わずに、さっさと宿題をやりなさい。
つべこべ
Stop arguing and just get on with your homework.
cf: ぶつぶつ is muttering complaints under your breath; つべこべ is arguing back with excuses.
cards.note: Almost always つべこべ言う in a command or scolding; rough and bossy.

cards.g: a handful; a tiny number (of people)
cards.d: 片手でつかめるくらいの量。また、ごくわずかな数。
s: そのことを知っているのは、社内でもほんの一握りの人間だけらしい。
一握り
Apparently only a handful of people in the company know about it.
プロとして成功できるのは、ほんの一握りの選手だけだ。
一握り
Only a tiny fraction of players ever make it as professionals.
cf: わずか is a general 'only a little'; 一握り is a vivid image used mostly for small elite groups.
cards.note: Literal sense: 一握りの米 'a handful of rice'.

cards.d: 銀色に光って見える、白くなった髪。
s: うちの課の権田部長は、銀髪をきっちりとなでつけた五十代後半の男だ。
銀髪
Gonda, head of our department, is a man in his late fifties with neatly slicked-back silver hair.
銀髪のおばあさんが、元気よく自転車をこいでいった。
銀髪
A silver-haired old lady pedalled briskly past on her bicycle.
cf: 白髪 (しらが) is neutral, often negative 'grey hair'; 銀髪 is flattering and stylish (also used for anime characters).

cards.d: 古い木や金属がこすれて出る、きしんだ音。
s: 部長が古い木の椅子にもたれかかると、椅子がぎいぎいと嫌な音を立てた。
ぎいぎい
When the boss leaned back in the old wooden chair, it gave a nasty creak.
風が吹くたびに、さびた門がぎいぎいと鳴る。
ぎいぎい
Every time the wind blows, the rusty gate creaks.
cf: ぎしぎし is a heavier creak (floors, joints); きいきい is a higher squeal (brakes, monkeys).
cards.note: Also written ギイギイ; a single creak is ぎいっ.

cards.d: わざとらしくなく、自然にふるまうようす。
s: 沖縄出身の比嘉くんがさりげなく彼女のグラスにお茶を注ぎ、「なんくるないさ」と笑った。
さりげな
Higa, who's from Okinawa, casually poured some tea into her glass and said with a grin, "Nankurunai sa — it'll be fine."
彼女のさりげない気づかいに、何度も助けられた。
さりげない
Her quiet, unfussy consideration has helped me many times.
cf: 何気ない = done without any particular intent; さりげない = deliberate but made to look casual (often a compliment).
cards.note: Adverb さりげなく is very common: さりげなく話題を変える 'casually change the subject'.

cards.g: for real, seriously (slang; usually written ガチ)
cards.d: 本気であること。冗談ではないこと。若者がよく使う。
s: 「は？　何それ、がちでうざいんだけど」
がち
"Huh? What's that supposed to mean? You're seriously annoying."
この店のラーメン、がちでうまいから一回食べてみて。
がち
The ramen here is seriously good — try it at least once.
cf: まじ (で) is the older, broader 'seriously'; がち(で) is newer and a notch stronger.
Not to be confused with the suffix 〜がち 'prone to' (忘れがち, 遅れがち).
cards.note: From ガチンコ (a real, no-holds-barred bout). Usually katakana ガチ. Source gloss 'diligent, honest' adjusted to the actual slang sense.

cards.g: to end up (having to do something unpleasant)
cards.d: 思ってもいなかった、困った立場に追いこまれる。
s: こうして僕は、面倒な役を一人で引き受ける羽目になった。
羽目になっ
And so I ended up stuck with the tedious job all by myself.
終電を逃して、駅から一時間歩いて帰る羽目になった。
羽目になっ
I missed the last train and ended up walking an hour home from the station.
cf: 羽目を外す means 'let loose, go overboard' — a different idiom with the same 羽目.
cards.note: Attached to a dictionary-form verb: 謝る羽目になる. Always for unwelcome outcomes.

cards.g: to contrive, devise artfully; mostly in 巧まざる 'artless, natural'
cards.d: 工夫をこらして、うまく作りあげる。
s: 巧まざるユーモアに見えたものは、実は入念に巧まれた芸だったわけだ。
巧まれ
What had looked like artless humour was in fact a carefully contrived act.
子どもの絵には、巧まずして生まれる美しさがある。
巧まずして
Children's drawings have a beauty that comes about without any artifice.
cf: たくらむ (企む) = scheme, often mischief; 巧む = craft skilfully.
巧み (たくみ) is the na-adjective 'skilful, clever' (巧みな話術).
cards.note: Rare as a plain verb; in practice you meet the negative 巧まざる/巧まずして ('unstudied, natural') in literary praise.

cards.g: extreme, gross, severe (usually of something bad)
cards.d: よくないことの程度が、とても大きい。
s: 母はいつも、うちの子どもたちは二人そろって生活の乱れが甚だしいと嘆いている。
甚だしい
Mum is forever lamenting that both her children lead extremely disorderly lives.
台風による農作物の被害は甚だしかった。
甚だし
The damage to crops from the typhoon was severe.
cf: 著しい is neutral 'marked, remarkable' (著しい成長); 甚だしい is almost always negative.
顕著 = conspicuous, clearly visible; no negative bias.
cards.note: 〜も甚だしい ('is a gross ~') is a set pattern for indignation: 誤解も甚だしい!

cards.g: if by any chance; in the unlikely event
cards.d: めったにないが、もしかしたら起こるかもしれない場合。
s: 「万が一ばれても、笑ったのは僕ってことにしとくから」
万が一
"If by any chance it comes out, I'll say it was me who laughed."
万が一に備えて、非常食と水を用意しておこう。
万が一
Let's keep emergency food and water ready, just in case.
cf: もしも is a general 'if'; 万が一 stresses that the case is unlikely (literally 'one in ten thousand').
念のため = 'to be on the safe side'; often paired: 万が一のために念のため…
cards.note: 万が一のことがあったら is a euphemism for death or serious accident.

cards.g: to exchange (words, looks, contracts); to cross
cards.d: おたがいにやりとりする。また、たがいに交差させる。
s: 二人がそっと目配せを交わすのを見て、僕も少しだけ肩の力が抜けた。
交わす
Seeing the two of them exchange a quiet glance, I relaxed a little too.
両社は来月、正式に契約を交わす予定だ。
交わす
The two companies are due to formally sign a contract next month.
cf: Homophone かわす (躱す) = dodge, sidestep (質問をかわす).
cards.note: Also as a suffix 〜交わす 'to each other': 語り交わす, 酌み交わす.

cards.d: はっきりと目立っていて、だれにでもわかるようす。
cards.reg: 書き言葉・報道・学術
s: その効果は顕著で、二次会に移る頃には課の空気がすっかりほぐれていた。
顕著
The effect was striking: by the time we moved on to the after-party, the whole section had loosened up.
高齢化の影響は、地方の小さな町で特に顕著に表れている。
顕著
The effects of population ageing are especially marked in small regional towns.
cf: Near-synonym; 著しい stresses degree (著しく低下), 顕著 stresses visibility (顕著な傾向).
甚だしい is negative 'extreme'; 顕著 is neutral.

cards.g: to disobey, go against (orders, expectations); to turn one's back on
cards.d: 決まりや言いつけ、期待などに逆らう。
s: 最近の美咲は何かと反抗的で、門限を守れという親の言いつけに背いては母と言い争っている。
背い
Lately Misaki has been defiant about everything, ignoring our parents' curfew and arguing with Mum.
親の期待に背いて、彼は大学をやめて料理人になった。
背い
Going against his parents' hopes, he quit university and became a cook.
cf: 逆らう is to resist or talk back directly; 背く is to act contrary to a rule, promise or expectation.
反抗的 describes the attitude; 背く is the act.
cards.note: Takes に: 命令に背く. 背 = back, as in turning your back on something.

cards.g: soon, before long; eventually (rare kanji for やがて)
cards.d: それほど時間がたたないうちに。そのうち。
s: 軈て終電の時間が近づき、部長は「気をつけて帰れよ」と一人ずつに声をかけて回った。
軈
Before long it was nearly time for the last train, and the boss went round telling each of us, "Get home safe."
春が来れば、この雪も軈て解けるだろう。
軈
When spring comes, this snow too will melt before long.
cf: まもなく = very soon (announcements: まもなく電車が参ります); やがて = after a while, in the natural course of things.
そのうち is casual and vague 'one of these days'.
cards.note: 軈 is a rare Japanese-made kanji; the word is almost always written やがて in kana, and 軈て appears mainly in older literature. The source gloss's 'almost, all but' are archaic senses — learn 'before long'.

title.ja: 単漢字 — 字の手ざわり
title.en: Single kanji: the feel of the character

modules.passageTitle: 一字の住まい — 漢字は熟語の中で暮らしている

cards.g: think, consider (archaic); in compounds: practice (稽古), comical (滑稽)
cards.d: もとは「考える」の意味。今は「けいこ」「こっけい」などの熟語に使う字。
s: 今では茶道や剣道の稽古のように、技を身につける練習を指す。
稽古
Today it means practice to master a skill, as in tea-ceremony or kendo training.
彼の大まじめな言い訳は、かえって滑稽に聞こえた。
滑稽
His dead-serious excuse only sounded comical.
cf: 考える is the modern verb for 'think'; 稽 survives almost only inside compounds.
cards.note: The kun reading かんが(える) for 稽 is archaic; you will not see it in modern prose. The source gloss 'quarrel' is not a Japanese usage and has been dropped. 稽古 is classically explained as 古(いにしえ)を稽(かんが)える, 'studying the ways of the past'.

cards.g: deep pool; abyss, depths; (fig.) the brink (絶望の淵)
cards.d: 川などで水が深くたまった所。追いつめられた状態のたとえにもなる。
s: 熟語では「深淵」として、のぞきこむのが怖いほどの深さを言う。
深淵
In the compound 深淵 it describes a depth so great you are afraid to look into it.
事業に失敗した彼は、一時は絶望の淵にいた。
絶望の淵
After his business failed, he was for a time in the depths of despair.
cf: 縁 (ふち) = rim, edge (眼鏡の縁, コップの縁); 淵 (ふち) = deep water. Same reading, unrelated meaning.
瀬 = shallows, rapids: the traditional opposite of 淵.
cards.note: Source reading omitted the common kun ふち. 'Edge' in the source gloss is misleading: rim/edge is 縁; 淵 is deep water, and 'brink' only in phrases like 絶望の淵. Also written with the variant 渕 in names.

compounds.en: ocean deep, deepest part of a trench

cards.r: フウ・フ ／ かぜ・かざ-
cards.d: 空気の流れ。また、ものごとの様子や、やり方・好み。
s: 空気の流れだけでなく、「風景」「風習」「和風」のように、土地の様子や暮らしのやり方まで表す。
風習
Beyond the movement of air, as in 風景, 風習 and 和風, it expresses the look of a place and even ways of living.
この旅館は古いけれど、なんとも言えない風情がある。
風情
This inn is old, but it has an indescribable charm.
cf: 〜風 (ふう) = 'in the style of / looking like' (学者風); 〜様 (よう) = 'like, as if'. 風 suggests outward appearance or manner.
cards.note: 風邪 is read かぜ as a whole (jukujikun). かざ- appears only in compounds like 風車 (かざぐるま, pinwheel) and 風上; 風車 read ふうしゃ is a windmill.

cards.r: リツ・ソツ ／ ひき(いる)
cards.g: rate, ratio, proportion (リツ); lead (ひきいる); rash, frank (ソツ compounds)
cards.d: 全体に対する割合。また、人の先に立って導くこと。
s: 同じ字でも「確率」はリツ、「引率」や「軽率」はソツと読み分ける。
確率
Even for the same character, you read it リツ in 確率 but ソツ in 引率 and 軽率.
修学旅行では、先生たちが生徒を引率して京都を回った。
引率
On the school trip, the teachers led the students around Kyoto.
cf: 割 is the everyday unit of tenths (一割 = 10%, 打率三割); 率 is the general/technical word for a rate.
cards.note: Readings: リツ for rates (確率, 比率, 効率, 打率); ソツ in 引率, 統率, 軽率, 率直 (そっちょく), 率先 (そっせん). Learn each compound's reading rather than a rule.

cards.r: ヨ ／ あま(る)・あま(す)
cards.g: surplus, remainder; over, more than (百余人); (archaic) I, myself
cards.d: 必要な分を超えて残ること。また、昔の言い方で「わたし」。
s: 「余白」「余裕」「余計」のどれにも、必要な分を超えて残ったものの気配がある。
余裕
In 余白, 余裕 and 余計 alike, there is a sense of something left over beyond what is needed.
余計なことを言って、かえって彼を怒らせてしまった。
余計
I said something unnecessary and ended up making him angry.
cf: 予 (ヨ, beforehand: 予定, 予約) shares the on'yomi; 予 was also an old first-person pronoun. 余 is the 'surplus' one.
cards.note: 余 = 'I' is archaic, heard today mainly from lords in period dramas (余は満足じゃ). As a suffix, 〜余 means 'a little over': 十年余.

cards.r: カツ ／ わ(る)・わり・さ(く)
cards.g: divide, split; tenth (10%); proportion; (〜の割に) considering
cards.d: ものをいくつかに分けること。また、十分の一を一つとする数え方。
s: 「一割」「割引」「分割」と並べてみると、全体をいくつかに分ける感覚が底に流れている。
割引
Line up 一割, 割引 and 分割, and you can feel an underlying sense of dividing a whole into parts.
時間の都合で、詳しい説明は割愛させていただきます。
割愛
Due to time constraints, I'll skip the detailed explanation.
cf: 率 is the general/technical rate (確率, 比率); 割 counts in tenths and is everyday (一割 = 10%).
cards.note: Verb readings: わる (to divide, break), さく (to spare time: 時間を割く). Sole on'yomi カツ appears in 分割 and 割愛.

cards.g: crime; offender; to commit (an offense, a mistake)
cards.d: 法や決まりを破ること。また、それをした人。
s: 「犯罪」「犯人」「防犯」と、ニュースでは毎日のように目にする字だ。
犯罪
As in 犯罪, 犯人 and 防犯, it is a character you see in the news practically every day.
この地域では、住民が交代で防犯パトロールをしている。
防犯
In this neighborhood, residents take turns doing crime-prevention patrols.
cf: 侵す (おかす) = to invade, infringe (領土・権利を侵す).
冒す (おかす) = to brave a risk (危険を冒す) or to afflict (病に冒される). 犯す = to break a law or commit an error.
cards.note: Sensitive: the verb 犯す also means 'to rape' when the object is a person. Counter suffix: 前科三犯 = three prior convictions.

cards.r: テン ／ まと(う)・まと(める)・まつ(わる)
cards.g: wear, wrap around oneself; gather, sum up; cling to, follow around
cards.d: 身にまきつけること。また、ばらばらのものを一つにすること。
s: それでも、江戸の火消しが掲げた「纏」や、職人の着る「半纏」には、この字がしっかり生きている。
半纏
Even so, the character is alive and well in the matoi standards raised by Edo firefighters and the hanten jackets worn by craftsmen.
見知らぬ男に付き纏われて、彼女は警察に相談した。
付き纏
Being followed around by a stranger, she went to the police.
cf: 着る is everyday 'wear'; 纏う is literary 'be clad in, wrap oneself in', often figurative (雰囲気を纏う).
cards.note: Not a jōyō kanji; まとめる, まとう, つきまとう are normally written in kana, so recognise 纏 mainly in 半纏, 纏 (まとい, a fire brigade's standard) and literary prose.

compounds.en: to follow around, stalk; to haunt
